title: Best Sudo Africa Alternatives for Card Issuing
summary: Compare the best Sudo Africa alternatives for card issuing. Evaluate APIs, supported markets, compliance, spend controls, pricing, and Miden's unified infrastructure.
body_markdown:
Sudo Africa is a sound place to start issuing cards in Nigeria. You get virtual and physical cards through APIs, without long bank negotiations.


The problems tend to arrive with scale. Cash sits idle across prefunded cards, approvals have to be fast at the point of sale, and your finance team ends up reconciling several providers for collections, FX, and payouts.


This guide compares six Sudo Africa alternatives on authorization, float, markets, and cost, so you can match a provider to where your program is heading.


## Key Takeaways


- The hard part of scaling a card program is rarely creating cards. It is trapped working capital, authorization response times, and reconciling several vendors.
- Marqeta and Lithic offer excellent real-time authorization tooling, but they require US or European entities and do not connect to African clearing rails such as NIP or M-Pesa.
- Maplerad, Anchor, and Flutterwave Issuing each cover a narrower slice, such as cross-border wallets, domestic Nigerian banking, or card add-ons for existing merchants. Cross-border treasury and card issuing stay split across providers.
- Miden suits scaling fintechs and enterprises that want cards, multi-currency accounts, treasury, and payouts on one ledger.


## Where Sudo Africa Fits, and Where Scaling Teams Look Further


Sudo Africa earned early traction with Nigerian developers by offering simple REST APIs for Verve, Mastercard, and Visa cards. For an MVP, basic spend limits, settlement accounts, and webhook callbacks are often all you need, and Sudo delivers them well.


As volumes grow, a few things deserve a closer look. The first is float. Sudo works mainly on a prefunded model, so money has to be set aside in each card balance before a transaction runs. On a corporate expense or fleet program, that can leave active cards short and trigger declines, or tie up working capital in idle balances across thousands of cards.


The second is how authorization decisions are made. Where a gateway funding model relies on your system answering a callback, response time matters, and a slow answer at checkout can turn into a decline. This applies to any callback model, so it is worth load-testing whichever provider you choose.


The third is scope. Sudo focuses on issuing, so collections, FX, and payouts typically come from other providers, and finance teams end up reconciling three or four sources each month. The fourth is cost. Sudo's pricing combines platform fees with per-authorization charges, which is worth modeling against your expected decline and retry rates if your margins are thin.

## 1. Miden


**Best For:** Fast-growing fintechs, cross-border platforms, and mid-market enterprises requiring high-availability card issuing unified with multi-currency accounts, automated treasury, and instant disbursements.


[Miden](https://www.miden.co/) is a Visa-partnered payments infrastructure provider. It treats card issuing as one part of a wider stack, sitting on top of its[Banking Stack](https://www.miden.co/banking-stack) ,[Global Treasury](https://www.miden.co/global-treasury) , and[Accruals & Disbursement](https://www.miden.co/accruals-disbursements) products.


Collections, FX, float management, and payouts run on one core ledger, so you do not need a separate banking relationship for each. When your application issues 10,000 cards, they draw on the same ledger that manages your float and vendor settlements.


### Miden’s Key Technical Capabilities


- **Dual-Mode Transaction Authorization:**


- **Miden-Managed:** Runs balance verification, MCC restrictions, velocity limits, and velocity-window fraud checks synchronously against rules configured in your dashboard.
- **Customer-Managed (Just-in-Time):** Dispatches an encrypted, HMAC-signed JSON callback containing the transaction amount, raw acquiring merchant data, ISO currency code, and cardholder metadata. Your service returns an explicit approve/decline payload within a strict sub-400ms SLA window.


- **Dynamic Treasury Funding:** Eliminates per-card prefunding by evaluating authorization against a shared, pooled multi-currency treasury account. Working capital stays centralized until the exact millisecond of authorization settlement.
- **BIN Routing & 3D Secure (3DS):** Issues across dual-currency corridors (NGN and USD). USD cards are provisioned on international BIN ranges compatible with major global SaaS, cloud, and advertising gateways (AWS, Meta Ads, Google Workspace), backed by programmable 3DS challenge webhooks rather than brittle, third-party SMS OTP portals.
- **Granular Spend Controls:** Enforce channel-level rule execution (ATM, web/e-commerce, POS), dynamic MCC whitelisting/blacklisting, single-transaction spend caps, and velocity throttles directly via the REST API.
- **Integrated Pan-African Rails:** Native multi-currency virtual accounts for collections (NGN and USD), local NIP bank transfers, and East African mobile money disbursements (M-Pesa) running on the same platform ledger.


### Pricing


Miden quotes pricing per program, based on volumes, card types, and currency corridors, and it is not publicly listed. Ask for per-transaction and FX terms early in scoping so you can model real unit costs.


### Considerations


Miden is architected for verified, production-grade businesses. Onboarding requires full KYB verification and an operational commitment to high-volume card issuing, making it unsuitable for informal testing, hobby projects, or low-volume MVPs.


### The Verdict


Miden is the clear choice for teams that have outgrown Sudo Africa’s prefunded float model and need real-time authorization control alongside consolidated multi-currency treasury.


[Talk to Miden's Expert Team](https://www.miden.co/contact) to structure your card program.


## 2. Maplerad (Wirefx)


**Best For:** Consumer remittance apps and cross-border platforms that prioritize multi-currency digital wallets alongside basic USD virtual card issuing.


Maplerad focuses on cross-border money movement. Through one API, platforms can create multi-currency wallets in NGN, USD, GHS, KES, and XAF, convert between them, and issue Visa virtual USD cards. Card creation requires customer verification, with pass or fail results returned by webhook.


### Features & Capabilities


- **Multi-Currency Wallets:** Assign virtual wallets in NGN, USD, GHS, KES, and XAF with programmatic conversion between balances.
- **Virtual USD Issuing:** Issues Visa virtual USD cards. Funding and defunding require calls to dedicated card balance endpoints.
- **Integrated KYC Flow:** Card generation requires customer identity verification, with pass or fail telemetry returned via webhook.


### Pricing


Custom quote / Not publicly disclosed.


### Considerations


Maplerad’s documented card support is limited to virtual USD cards, so domestic NGN debit cards and branded physical programs are not covered. Cards are funded and defunded through dedicated balance endpoints instead of drawing dynamically from a central balance. Card interchange, cross-border surcharges, and wallet funding costs are invoiced through monthly statements, which leaves reconciliation to your finance team.


### The Verdict


Maplerad is a competent option for software companies focused on cross-border USD wallet spending. If you need physical cards, domestic currency clearing, or card liquidity tied to a treasury balance, you will need a broader platform like Miden.


## 3. Anchor


**Best For:** Nigerian fintechs and digital consumer apps seeking a localized Banking-as-a-Service provider for domestic deposit accounts and basic debit cards.


Anchor is a Lagos-based BaaS provider integrated with CBN-licensed partner banks. It is built for domestic neobanks, savings apps, and wallets that run on Nigerian Interbank Settlement System rails.


It offers naira debit cards across Verve, Mastercard, and Visa, plus virtual USD cards, along with virtual NIP accounts, deposit sub-accounts, bulk transfers, and bill payments. For cardholder security, PAN and CVV are retrieved through time-limited tokenized endpoints with a 5-minute reveal window.


### Features & Capabilities


- **Domestic Card Configurations:** Offers naira debit cards supported across Verve, Mastercard, and Visa, along with virtual USD cards.
- **Core BaaS Capabilities:** Provides virtual NIP accounts, deposit sub-accounts, bulk bank transfers, and local bill payment infrastructure.
- **Cardholder Security:** Utilizes time-limited tokenized endpoints with a 5-minute reveal window for retrieving PAN and CVV details.


### Pricing


Custom quote / Not publicly disclosed.


### Considerations


Anchor is tied to the Nigerian domestic banking system and does not offer issuing in Kenya, Tanzania, or Sierra Leone. It also does not publicly expose sub-second, customer-managed authorization webhooks, so you cannot run your own balance and fraud logic at the transaction edge. Multi-currency liquidity management and automated cross-border payouts are limited as well.


### The Verdict


Anchor suits projects that begin and end within Nigerian consumer banking. If you plan to expand across borders or need tight control over authorization, you will likely outgrow it.


## 4. Flutterwave Issuing


**Best For:** Existing Flutterwave merchants that need to spin up basic, prefunded expense cards directly from their merchant gateway balances.


Flutterwave Issuing lets businesses on Flutterwave's payment gateway create virtual and physical cards funded from their merchant settlement accounts. It works as an add-on to Flutterwave's acquiring products.


You can fund NGN and USD virtual cards from existing collections balances, including debiting an NGN balance to fund a USD card, and issue cards through the dashboard or the API with basic spend limits.


### Features & Capabilities


- **Merchant Balance Funding:** Fund virtual NGN and USD cards directly from existing merchant collections balances.
- **Dashboard Spend Tools:** Issue cards manually through a web dashboard or programmatically via API, with options for basic spend limits.
- **Cross-Currency Balance Pulls:** Debit an NGN merchant settlement balance to fund a USD virtual card.


### Pricing


Custom quote / Not publicly disclosed.


### Considerations


The virtual naira cards are tuned for merchants already inside the Flutterwave ecosystem, which limits general-purpose use. Flutterwave also controls authorization end to end, so developers cannot intercept transactions with low-latency callbacks to apply custom underwriting, dynamic balances, or fraud rules.


### The Verdict


Flutterwave Issuing works well as an operating expense tool for businesses already processing payments through Flutterwave. For user-facing, high-volume card products that need custom authorization and dedicated infrastructure, you may want more control than the product currently documents.


## 5. Marqeta


**Best For:** Scale-ups and multinational enterprises with verified North American or European legal entities requiring industry-standard dynamic authorization logic.


Marqeta is publicly traded on NASDAQ and is a global standard for card issuing and transaction processing, powering programs for companies such as DoorDash and Klarna. Its just-in-time funding keeps cards at zero balance and funds them at the moment of purchase, through either Managed JIT or Gateway JIT. Program controls cover MCCs, geofencing, and spending velocity, and the company emphasizes enterprise uptime backed by SLAs.


### Features & Capabilities


- **Just-in-Time (JIT) Funding:** Zero-balance card architecture that issues real-time authorization callbacks through Managed JIT and Gateway JIT, funding the card only at the exact millisecond of purchase.
- **Configurable Program Controls:** Deep, programmatic rule configurations governing MCCs, geographical geo-fencing, and cardholder spending velocities.
- **Enterprise Uptime:** Documented 99.99% core engine uptime backed by institutional SLAs.


### Pricing


Custom quote / Not publicly disclosed.


### Considerations


Marqeta does not connect to African payment rails or local identity databases. Deployment requires corporate registration, banking relationships, and regulatory standing in the US, UK, or Europe, and programs typically involve a significant engineering commitment and minimum volume commitments. Those requirements put it out of reach for most regional African businesses.


### The Verdict


Marqeta is an excellent issuing engine for Western jurisdictions. Without African rails, though, it cannot serve domestic issuing on the continent. Miden offers a similar dynamic-authorization approach for African and multi-currency corridors.


## 6. Lithic


**Best For:** US-incorporated engineering teams looking for rapid, developer-first card issuing APIs with deep code-level spend controls.


Lithic is a developer-focused card issuing platform known for clear documentation, public SDKs, a CLI, and quick test deployments. Its authorization rules let you write conditional logic around merchant category, velocity, time of day, and geolocation. Apple Pay and Google Pay provisioning is available directly through API endpoints.


### Features & Capabilities


- **Programmatic Auth Rules:** Fine-grained code-level control over transaction authorizations via conditional logic based on merchant category, velocity, time of day, and geolocation.
- **Developer Tooling:** Public SDKs, open API specifications, fast sandbox deployment, and automated testing tools.
- **Tokenization & Mobile Wallets:** Native support for Apple Pay and Google Pay provisioning directly through API endpoints.


### Pricing


Custom quote / Not publicly disclosed.


### Considerations


Lithic is built around the US financial system, so it cannot issue cards in African domestic currencies or settle through regional payment rails. It also requires a verified US corporate structure, which limits its relevance for businesses operating in Africa.


### The Verdict


Lithic is one of the cleanest developer APIs for launching cards in the United States. For platforms that operate in emerging markets or need local currency settlement, it does not fit. Miden offers programmatic control designed around African and cross-border operations.


## What to Check Before You Choose a Card-Issuing Provider


Do not choose a card provider based on marketing claims or basic card-creation speed. Focus on these four operational checkpoints.


1. Real-Time Authorization vs. Trapped Card Float


Prefunding means locking money into card balances before anyone can spend. Idle cards hold cash while busy cards risk declines when their balances run dry. Dynamic funding keeps cards at zero until a purchase happens, then funds it from a central pool at that moment.


Miden supports this with signed authorization callbacks answered in under 400ms, drawing from your treasury pool only when a transaction occurs.


[Launch dynamic cards with Miden](https://www.miden.co/cards)


1. Multi-Currency Treasury vs. Liquidity Delays


If you issue USD cards in Africa, dollar supply is often the biggest operational risk. Gateways that rely on third-party currency brokers can see USD cards freeze or carry steep markups when FX gets tight.


Miden builds card issuing on its Global Treasury engine, which gives you continuous NGN and USD liquidity and reduces your exposure to sudden shortages and wide spreads.


1. One ledger versus several vendors


A card API covers one part of the cash cycle. You still need accounts for collections, tools for FX, and payout rails for vendors. Each extra provider adds engineering hours and makes month-end reconciliation harder. Miden handles deposits, virtual cards, corporate expense cards, and bank payouts on one reconciled ledger.


[Consolidate your stack on Miden](https://www.miden.co/banking-stack)


1. Real Total Cost of Ownership


Card creation fees are only part of the picture. Add monthly maintenance fees, per-authorization charges on failed attempts, wallet funding costs, and the accounting hours spent chasing unmatched transactions. Ask every provider for per-attempt, FX, and funding terms in writing.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What makes Miden different from Sudo Africa?


Sudo is an issuing layer that works mainly on prefunded balances. Miden pairs virtual and physical card issuing with multi-currency accounts, treasury, and disbursements on a single ledger. It supports both managed and customer-managed authorization, with response times under 400ms.


### Is Sudo Africa good for card issuing?


Yes, for getting started. Sudo provides virtual and physical cards through accessible APIs, which suits MVPs and early programs. Teams usually look at alternatives like Miden when float, authorization control, or the number of vendors they reconcile starts to slow them down.


### Can Miden issue physical and virtual cards across multiple currencies?


Yes. Miden provides APIs for custom-branded virtual cards and for physical Retail, Corporate, and Corporate Lite cards. Issuance and settlement run in NGN and USD, with regional infrastructure across Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, and Sierra Leone.


### Why can't African platforms simply use Marqeta or Lithic?


Both are strong processors, but they work through US, UK, or European banking infrastructure and require entities in those jurisdictions. They do not support African clearing rails such as NIP or M-Pesa, local currency settlement, or regional identity checks like BVN and NIN.


### How does one platform reduce reconciliation costs?


When collections, FX, cards, and payouts sit with different vendors, transactions settle on different schedules across separate ledgers. On Miden, inflows, card transactions, currency conversions, and disbursements reconcile on one ledger, which cuts manual accounting work.
